thread:
maria: Heads-up — we've had 3 separate customers in the last 6 hours with OAuth failures: `state mismatch` on Google and GitHub logins. They all use our SPA deep-link redirect (example `https://app.customer.com/#/oauth/callback...`) and some go through a CDN/proxy. Repro attached below.

alex: Fragments (the part after `#`) are never sent to the server by browsers. If the app is sticking the code/state in the hash, the backend will never see it — that would cause a state mismatch.

jordan: I grabbed one of the customer's redirect examples: `https://app.customer.com/%23/oauth/callback?state=abc+123&code=...` — note the `%23` (encoded `#`). After passing through their proxy it shows up in our logs as `https://app.customer.com/?code=...&state=abc%20123` (plus -> space). Looks like the proxy or URL-decoder is turning `+` into spaces.

sam: Yep, `+` -> space is expected for application/x-www-form-urlencoded decoding. If the client encoded the state with `+` for spaces rather than using base64url, that can break when proxies re-decode.

maria: Example server-side log (redacted):
```
Incoming GET /?code=SplxlOBeZQQYbYS6WxSbIA&state=abc%20123 from 34.56.78.90
Session[state] = "abc+123"
--> result: state mismatch, 403
```

alex: Two separate issues colliding: (1) hash vs query — fragments don't reach our server; (2) state encoding/decoding across proxies (`+` vs `%20`). Both can independently cause state mismatch.

jordan: Repro steps I used (fast):
1) Run a simple SPA that redirects to `/#/oauth/callback?state=<urlencoded state>`
2) Start a local proxy that does a `decodeURIComponent` on path parts then forwards
3) Trigger OAuth with GitHub (response_type=code)
4) Observe backend receives `state` with spaces instead of `+`, compare fails

sam: Quick mitigations:
- Ask customers to change redirect to not include a hash (use path-based redirect: `/oauth/callback`), and ensure the OAuth app's redirect URI matches exactly.
- Recommend encoding state with base64url (no `+` `/` `=`) so proxies won't mangle it.
- For server-side tolerance, we can normalize incoming state by replacing spaces with `+` before validating (low risk if paired with stricter checks), but that reduces strictness.

support_bot: FYI — added incident tag `oauth-state-encoding` and assigned to eng-oncall. :rotating_light:

maria: Can engineering evaluate a short-lived tolerant fix (space->plus normalization) while we notify customers and update docs? One affected customer is blocked on SSO for a pilot.

alex: I can put a small middleware change behind a feature flag: normalize `req.query.state` by reverting ` ` -> `+` and also try a base64url decode fallback. I'll open a PR with tests.

jordan: Also add a debug log that records the raw `req.originalUrl` and `Referer` for these flows so we can follow the next incident. Keep it minimal and redact tokens.

maria: Thanks — please cc me on the PR and I'll tell the customers the expected config change (no `#` in redirect, use path-based redirect, use base64url for state). :thumbsup:

sam: One more note — for mobile in-app webviews, confirm they don't transform `#` behavior (WKWebView sometimes rewrites URLs in deep links). If a customer uses an SDK that manipulates the URL fragment, they'll need to surface state to the server explicitly (postMessage or query param).

alex: Agreed. I'll include mobile webview guidance in the PR description.

maria: 👍 closing loop after PR + customer notif.
